title: Todd Blanche Confirmed as Attorney General
description_short: The Senate narrowly confirmed Todd Blanche as AG by 50-49 vote. Confirmation drew sharp criticism over DOJ independence and use against political opponents.
description_medium: The Senate confirmed Todd Blanche as attorney general by a 50–49 vote on August 8, 2026, after weeks of uncertainty. Blanche had been Donald Trump’s personal lawyer. Two Republican senators, Susan Collins and Lisa Murkowski, joined Democrats in opposing him. The confirmation drew scrutiny over his role in a controversial IRS settlement and concerns about Justice Department independence.
description_long: The Senate confirmed Todd Blanche as the nation’s attorney general by a 50–49 vote in the early hours of August 8, 2026. Blanche had previously served as Donald Trump’s personal attorney, and senators from both parties had raised concerns about his role in a controversial IRS settlement involving the president. All Democrats voted against the confirmation, joined by Republican senators Susan Collins and Lisa Murkowski. The vote followed weeks of uncertainty and a late-night session that continued past 4 a.m. Blanche said he was honored by Trump’s confidence and thanked the Senate for completing the process. The linked report describes criticism over the Justice Department’s independence and the potential for its powers to be used against political opponents. It does not establish how Blanche would handle particular investigations or what impact his confirmation would have on DOJ policy. The confirmed vote and the concerns raised during review are documented; their effect on the department’s future conduct remained unresolved at the time of the report.
subcategory: Attorney general confirmation and DOJ independence
notes: Added the vote date, margin, named Republican opponents and the concerns reported during confirmation; kept the future effect on DOJ independence unresolved.

title: Brain Tumor Girl Deported to Mexico; DHS Denies Family Humanitarian Parole in 2026
description_short: Brain Tumor Girl Deported to Mexico; DHS Denies Family Humanitarian Parole in 2026
description_medium: NBC News reported that a U.S.-citizen child with a brain tumor went to Mexico with her undocumented parents after they were deported in February 2025. By 2026, her family said her condition had worsened without access to specialized care, and DHS denied the family’s humanitarian-parole request in May. Her doctors warned that the tumor could return; the medical claims are attributed to the family and clinicians.
description_long: NBC News reported that immigration authorities deported a girl’s undocumented parents to Mexico in February 2025 and that the U.S.-citizen child went with them, along with her siblings. The family said agents detained them at a Texas checkpoint while they were traveling to the girl’s Houston specialist. The child had been treated for a rare brain tumor. By February 2026, her family said her recovery had stalled and that she could no longer write or speak in full sentences while living without access to her specialized care. DHS denied the family’s humanitarian-parole request in May 2026 without giving an explanation, according to the supplied account. The girl’s U.S. doctors warned that the tumor could return. These details describe the family’s account and medical concerns reported to NBC; they do not establish a new diagnosis or the agency’s rationale for denying parole. The title says the U.S.-citizen girl was deported, while the report says her parents were deported and she went with them. That distinction should be corrected before the entry is marked complete.
notes: Needs context: NBC reports that the U.S.-citizen child went to Mexico with her parents after they were deported; the title says the child herself was deported. Medical deterioration and tumor risk are attributed to the family and her doctors, and DHS’s reason for denying parole is not supplied.
Proposed correction: Revise the title to say the child accompanied her deported parents, and retain attribution for the family’s account and physicians’ medical concerns.

title: The Trump administration designats Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his government allies
description_short: The Trump administration designats Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his government allies as members of a foreign terrorist organization
description_medium: The Trump administration designated the “Cartel de los Soles” as a foreign terrorist organization, while identifying Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and government allies as members, CNN reported in November 2025. Experts quoted by CNN disputed whether the name described a conventional organized-crime group. The designation enabled sanctions but did not explicitly authorize lethal force, according to legal experts.
description_long: CNN reported that the Trump administration formally designated the “Cartel de los Soles” as a foreign terrorist organization in November 2025 and identified Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and government allies as members. The designation took effect on November 24. Experts told CNN that the phrase was often used to describe alleged corruption among Venezuelan officials rather than a conventional, centralized criminal organization, and Maduro’s government denied the group existed. Legal experts said the designation could support sanctions against Maduro’s assets and infrastructure but did not itself explicitly authorize lethal force. Administration officials argued that it could expand military options, while U.S. forces had already been conducting an anti-drug campaign in the region. The report therefore distinguishes the formal designation of the named entity from the administration’s claims about Maduro’s membership and from possible military action. It does not establish that the designation alone authorized strikes or that the allegations about the group were proven. The supplied category of disinformation is not explained by the source; the account is about a contested terrorism designation and its possible consequences.
notes: Corrected the description to distinguish the named organization’s designation from the administration’s claim that Maduro was a member; preserved uncertainty about the alleged group and the designation’s effect on military authority.
